video_title: LaMelo Ball Joins ANT in CRAZY Wolves Trade, Jalen Brown vs. ESPN | Was Miles Bridges TOXIC for CHA?

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on the Timberwolves' trade for LaMelo Ball
quotes.excerpt: Watch the championship this year and gave away your second-best player and he goes on to win
quotes.quote: Watch the championship this year and gave away your second-best player and he goes on to win the championship and that desperation starts to kick in because you got a young star who if they don't make these moves, he could be looking at not being in Minnesota long-term. So that's a great move and keeping the young superstar happy.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Wosny Lambre and Danny Green on the Hornets' lack of winning mentality
quotes.excerpt: Always remember that. They don't have a winning mentality this year.

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: But you still have to be a team to win. There's a lot of people as good as, I'm saying, that doesn't mean he's going to win a championship.

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: Also Charlotte, as you can see by the move, they don't want to win. Always remember that. They don't have a winning mentality this year.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on Jalen Brown's MVP candidacy and influence
quotes.excerpt: Jalen Brown was an MVP candidate. There's one thing you can't say about Jalen Brown, he influences winning.
quotes.quote: Jalen Brown was an MVP candidate. Now, you're saying, does he do the things that Luka and Wemby do? Okay, yeah, the stats on these guys are going to look a little different. But there's one thing you can't say about Jalen Brown, he influences winning. I don't know what you got to say about that.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Wosny Lambre on the Hornets' trade with the Timberwolves
quotes.excerpt: First, they traded LaMelo Ball and Josh Green to the Minnesota Timberwolves in exchange for Naz Reid.
quotes.quote: The Charlotte Hornets guys are cleaning house. They gave some pink slips out this week. First, they traded LaMelo Ball and Josh Green to the Minnesota Timberwolves in exchange for Naz Reid. The Wolves 2033 unprotected first-round pick, three pick swaps, and three second-round picks. It sounds like a lot, but really, two of those pick swaps are like nothing. And then the third pick swap is like the third, it's like a swap they've already swapped, and they just like decrease the order, so it's like whatever. Three second-round picks, and after the trade, the Minnesota Timberwolves championship odds actually shot up.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Wosny Lambre on the Suns' acquisition of Grayson Allen and Royce O'Neale
quotes.excerpt: Also, they traded away Miles Bridges and a 2029 first-round pick to the Phoenix Suns.
quotes.quote: Also, they traded away Miles Bridges and a 2029 first-round pick and a 2027 second-round pick to the Phoenix Suns for Grayson Allen, Royce O'Neale, and a 2033 first-round pick.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on the Timberwolves' need to keep their young star happy
quotes.excerpt: The Wolves had to do something, I believe. Whatever that is to keep their young superstar happy.
quotes.quote: The Wolves had to do something, I believe. Whatever that is to keep their young superstar happy. They had to somehow try to get better and, you know, when you add another All-Star in LaMelo Ball, when you watch the championship this year and gave away your second-best player and he goes on to win the championship and cat, Carl-Anthony Towns, I'm talking about for the Knicks, it's like desperation starts to kick in because you got a young star who if they don't make these moves, he could be looking at like not being in Minnesota long-term. So that's a great move and, you know, keeping the young superstar happy.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on the Hornets' culture change
quotes.excerpt: I look at this as like a culture change for them. You know, they got to rid of some guys.
quotes.quote: I look at this as like a culture change for them. You know, they got to rid of some guys in LaMelo and Bridges who were their stars, a little older than what they can build around now with like Brandon Miller and Nick Smith Jr. and just kind of just cleaning house and opened up some cap space so they can, they can be in a sweepstakes for, you know, a key free agent.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green on the Timberwolves' roster depth after the trade
quotes.excerpt: I like LaMelo personally. I think he's a good basketball player. It helps with the double team.
quotes.quote: I like LaMelo personally. I think he's a good basketball player. I think he's exciting, he's entertaining. It helps with the double team some for Anthony Edwards, but I don't know if they got better. Like they got rid of your bigs, one, two stretch four, stretch five bigs, and you only have as Rudy now. So their bench, their depth lineup, it just very thin. Now, those guys are scorers, they can score, but Dante's not there, so you don't have a bunch of shooters around them either. So you have IOD, you have LaMelo, you have Anthony Edwards, they all capable of knocking down threes, but they're not shooters, they're scorers. And they're mostly need the ball in the hands to get downhill to give them more space. It's not going to be Rudy, and you know, Jalen McDaniels is a solid shooter, but you need like shooters to give those guys space to operate, I feel like.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on Jalen Brunson's defensive impact
quotes.excerpt: He's never shown that he's the kind of player that could make a huge impact.
quotes.quote: He's never shown that he's the kind of player that could make a huge impact in say the Spurs series they played in last year or the OKC series they played in the year before that. I think for this to be worth what they did, he's got to be a different kind of player, which he's never shown in terms of taking it deadly serious on defense. Not to say you got to come out and be Scotty Pippen, but like you got to be credible. Right? Like we talked about Jalen Brunson in the playoffs this year where he's traditionally been the Knicks' weak point. He made himself into somebody that's like, look, I'm not going to be able to guard Stefan Castle, but you put me on Shin Penny, I'm doing that hedge and recover extremely hard and I'm executing it every single play. And then when I do get caught up in a switch, sometimes I'm taking the charge, sometimes like he made himself into the best version of defender that he could be.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on the Timberwolves' reliance on Anthony Edwards
quotes.excerpt: I think Minnesota management is kind of counting on Ant and his ability to shape culture.
quotes.quote: I think Minnesota management is kind of counting on Ant and his ability to shape culture and get LaMelo to be a different person than he's seen. Because if he's just the same dude that he was in Charlotte, I don't know why this is worth what you did. Even if, you know, you talked about the double teams and stuff like that, I think their offense completely changes. Like it's going to be way harder to do that double team at the top to Ant when he's not even on the ball. Like now it's just like LaMelo is the point guard and, you know, I think they've helped their offense a lot, but like you said, they're very thin up front.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green on LaMelo Ball's injury history and team impact
quotes.excerpt: And LaMelo also, again, he had his probably career high in games played this past year.
quotes.quote: And LaMelo also, again, he had his probably career high in games played this past year. And they had to move him to the bench with the minute restriction. They had to come, take him off the bench and like, so most of the years he's probably averaged about 55 games, I guess, prior to this. So you're banking a lot on him and Anthony Edwards being healthy for the most of the time. If they're not, without those guys being healthy, this team is like a play-in team.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on the Timberwolves' status as a play-in team
quotes.excerpt: If they're not healthy for 60 games of the year, this is a play-in team.
quotes.quote: If they're not healthy for 60 games of the year, this is a play-in team.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green on the Timberwolves' roster limitations
quotes.excerpt: If he plays 46 games and say Anthony Edwards is healthy all those games, this is a play-in team.
quotes.quote: If he plays 46 games and say Anthony Edwards is healthy all those games, this is a play-in team. That's what I'm saying. And I'm not saying like, but LaMelo's missed a lot of games. And this past year, Ant had missed a good amount of games. They got to play, yeah. And I'm not saying both at the same time. If one of them is out, they're not winning a lot of games. That is a play-in team.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on LaMelo Ball's injury history
quotes.excerpt: Has he had any major injuries? Like what was his major injury?
quotes.quote: Has he had any major injuries? Like what was his major injury?

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green on LaMelo Ball's injury history
quotes.excerpt: Ankles and like, ankles mostly. I think strains. He might have had a calf strain.
quotes.quote: Ankles and like, ankles mostly. I think strains. He might have had a calf strain. I don't think he like tore anything, like he might have, he might have. Ankles, nothing like, nothing like no surgery really. I mean, so again, it wasn't like Aaron Gordon where it was tendons.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on the impact of tanking on player availability
quotes.excerpt: Also with the missed games, we also got to take into account when your team is tanking.
quotes.quote: Also with the missed games, we also got to take into account when your team is tanking, they're not rushing you back for games. When you have nothing to play for and the incentive is like, we can go out and get Con Cunnipole and Brandon Miller, they're like, take your time coming back from these injuries. Like that, like this year they were playing for shit and he actually played a lot, right? So, you know, they had to go to more restriction for him to play those 70 games.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on LaMelo Ball's injury reputation
quotes.excerpt: I'm just saying even with the injuries, when you playing on a team that's trying to lose.
quotes.quote: I'm just saying even with the injuries, when you playing on a team that's trying to lose every freaking game, they tell your best player, don't play.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on Julius Randle's performance
quotes.excerpt: You've seen that two years in a row, like whether that was against OKC, whether that was against the Spurs.
quotes.quote: You've seen that two years in a row, like whether that was against OKC, whether that was against the Spurs, he just wasn't good enough. So if you know, why not take a shot on somebody who's ultra talented and think if you get him in your building, you'll get more out of him.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on the Hornets' trade of LaMelo Ball
quotes.excerpt: LaMelo Ball has always been somebody who's asked to drive offense, drive his team.
quotes.quote: LaMelo Ball has always been somebody who's asked to drive offense, drive his team. Charlotte's offense, like you look at the on-off numbers, like people would just like, oh LaMelo shot this. I'm like, bro, when he was on the court, that offense was different. And it's because of him. It's because he was driving that with the creativity and the playmaking and, you know, the threat from three and all of that kind of stuff. Jaylen Brown, I think he's an ultimate winning player, he's guarded the best wings for them, blah, blah, blah, had 40 points in the finals. He's never had to do that for nobody's offense in his life. He's never been some number one guy. Yo, Jaylen, go save us. That's never been his job. So like, I think, look, I understand people's problems with LaMelo Ball. Like 20 seconds left on the shot clock, you take a 35-footer, that shit misses. It's like, goddamn, bro.
